events.title: Webster–Ashburton Treaty Signed
events.description: US Secretary of State Daniel Webster and Britain's Lord Ashburton signed a treaty that settled long-running border disputes between the United States and British North America. It fixed the boundary between Maine and New Brunswick, among other points.
events.significance: The treaty defused tensions that might have led to war. It also set the course for peaceful relations between the US and Britain in the century that followed.

events.title: Jesse Owens Wins His Fourth Gold Medal in Berlin
events.description: Jesse Owens ran the opening leg of the American 4x100-meter relay team at the Berlin Olympics. The team set a world record and won gold. It was his fourth gold medal of the Games.
events.significance: Owens' victories in Nazi Germany undercut the regime's claims of racial superiority. They made him one of the most celebrated athletes in history.

events.title: Atomic Bomb Dropped on Nagasaki
events.description: Three days after Hiroshima, a US B-29 bomber named Bockscar dropped a plutonium bomb called "Fat Man" on Nagasaki, Japan. Tens of thousands of people were killed.
events.significance: This was the second and last use of a nuclear weapon in war. It came just before Japan's surrender and the end of World War II.

events.title: Richard Nixon Resigns the Presidency
events.description: Following the Watergate scandal, Richard Nixon became the first US president to resign. Vice President Gerald Ford was sworn in as his successor.
events.significance: The resignation tested the US constitutional system and shaped public attitudes toward government and political accountability for decades.

events.title: Composer Dmitri Shostakovich Dies
events.description: Dmitri Shostakovich died in Moscow at age 68 after a battle with lung cancer. He was one of the most acclaimed Russian composers of the 20th century. His symphonies and string quartets were written under the pressures of Soviet rule.
events.significance: His music remains widely performed. It is often heard as a powerful record of life under political repression.
